ne-50ced078.stem: Which cranial nerve supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius?
ne-50ced078.explanation: The accessory nerve leaves through the jugular foramen, pierces sternocleidomastoid and crosses the posterior triangle of the neck to reach trapezius. It can be injured in the posterior triangle during neck dissection.

ne-c94694b2.stem: Which cranial nerve gives parasympathetic fibres to most of the thoracic and abdominal organs?
ne-c94694b2.explanation: The vagus nerve has the longest course of any cranial nerve; it gives parasympathetic fibres to the heart, lungs and digestive tract (up to about the left third of the transverse colon).

ne-34dda1f9.stem: Which nerve carries hearing and balance?
ne-34dda1f9.explanation: The cochlear part of the vestibulocochlear nerve carries hearing and the vestibular part carries balance. It passes through the internal acoustic meatus together with the facial nerve.

ne-667ba770.stem: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
ne-667ba770.explanation: There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal. Although there are 7 cervical vertebrae, there are 8 cervical nerves.

ne-15f8e734.stem: The brachial plexus is formed by the anterior rami of which spinal nerves?
ne-15f8e734.explanation: The brachial plexus is formed by the anterior rami of C5–T1 and is organised into roots, trunks, divisions, cords and branches; it provides all motor and sensory innervation of the upper limb.

ne-26e018da.stem: What is the motor nerve of the diaphragm?
ne-26e018da.explanation: The phrenic nerve descends in the neck on the front of scalenus anterior and supplies the diaphragm. Pain from the diaphragm is referred to the shoulder, the dermatome of the same segments.

ne-d86f39c7.stem: Which is the thickest and longest nerve in the body?
ne-d86f39c7.explanation: The sciatic nerve comes from the L4–S3 roots, leaves through the greater sciatic foramen and descends in the back of the thigh; it usually divides above the popliteal fossa into the tibial and common fibular nerves.

ne-da1e6de1.stem: Which nerve supplies the anterior muscles of the thigh (quadriceps femoris)?
ne-da1e6de1.explanation: The femoral nerve (L2–L4) passes into the thigh through the muscular lacuna and supplies quadriceps femoris, sartorius and pectineus; when it is damaged, knee extension and the patellar reflex are lost.

ne-63d6ca4d.stem: Which nerve supplies most of the medial (adductor) muscles of the thigh?
ne-63d6ca4d.explanation: The obturator nerve (L2–L4) passes through the obturator canal into the medial compartment of the thigh and supplies most of the adductors; the hamstring part of adductor magnus is supplied by the sciatic nerve.

ne-6c143cec.stem: Which nerve is compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome?
ne-6c143cec.explanation: At the wrist the median nerve passes under the flexor retinaculum through the carpal tunnel together with the flexor tendons. Compression causes numbness in the first three and a half fingers and weakness of the thenar muscles.

ne-8a555c3e.stem: Which nerve causes tingling on the little-finger side of the hand when the inner side of the elbow is knocked?
options: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm
ne-8a555c3e.explanation: At the elbow the ulnar nerve runs just under the skin behind the medial epicondyle (the 'funny bone'). A blow or compression causes tingling in the 4th and 5th fingers.

ne-4bd49a5e.stem: Which nerve supplies triceps brachii, the posterior muscle of the arm?
ne-4bd49a5e.explanation: The radial nerve supplies all the posterior (extensor) muscles of the arm and forearm. In fractures of the shaft of the humerus it can be injured in the radial groove, causing wrist drop.

ne-d2881471.explanation: The axillary nerve (C5–C6) winds around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies deltoid and teres minor. It can be injured in fractures of the surgical neck and in shoulder dislocations.

ne-4eef8b32.stem: In which segments of the spinal cord are the cell bodies of the sympathetic preganglionic neurons?
ne-4eef8b32.explanation: The sympathetic system has a thoracolumbar outflow: the preganglionic neurons lie in the lateral horn of segments T1–L2. Their fibres reach the sympathetic trunk through the ventral root and the white ramus communicans.

ne-8691959b.stem: From which regions do the fibres of the parasympathetic system arise?
options: Brainstem (III, VII, IX, X) and S2–S4 (craniosacral)
ne-8691959b.explanation: The parasympathetic system has a craniosacral outflow: it is distributed through cranial nerves III, VII, IX and X and through the pelvic splanchnic nerves from segments S2–S4.

ne-11836b1d.stem: How does the pupil change in the 'fight or flight' response, and which system does this?
options: It does not change – somatic system
ne-11836b1d.explanation: Sympathetic stimulation contracts dilator pupillae and widens the pupil. Parasympathetic fibres (oculomotor nerve) constrict the pupil through sphincter pupillae.

ne-aca0bd08.stem: The cell bodies of which neurons are found in the spinal ganglion?
ne-aca0bd08.explanation: The spinal ganglion on the dorsal root contains the pseudounipolar neurons that carry sensation from the periphery to the spinal cord; there are no synapses in this ganglion.

ne-d5797703.stem: By which branch do the preganglionic fibres to the sympathetic trunk ganglia leave the spinal nerve?
ne-d5797703.explanation: Myelinated preganglionic fibres enter the sympathetic trunk through the white ramus communicans (present only at T1–L2). Unmyelinated postganglionic fibres return to the spinal nerve through the grey ramus communicans.

ne-4d840655.stem: Through which opening does the pudendal nerve leave the pelvis, and through which does it enter the perineum?
options: Leaves through the greater sciatic foramen, enters through the inguinal canal
Leaves through the obturator canal, enters through the lesser sciatic foramen
Leaves through the sacral hiatus, enters through the lesser sciatic foramen
Leaves through the greater sciatic foramen, enters through the lesser sciatic foramen
Leaves through the lesser sciatic foramen, enters through the greater sciatic foramen
ne-4d840655.explanation: The pudendal nerve (S2–S4) leaves the pelvis below piriformis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks behind the sacrospinous ligament and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen, running on in the pudendal canal (Alcock).

ne-7a6e6c80.stem: Where is the common fibular nerve most often injured?
options: Around the neck of the fibula
ne-7a6e6c80.explanation: The common fibular nerve runs superficially just below the head of the fibula, winding around its neck. A fracture, pressure from a plaster cast or sitting cross-legged can damage the nerve here and cause foot drop.
